rgb: Viewed from a sharply downward-facing egocentric perspective, the camera wearer is looking at a padded beige-and-grey armrest approximately 0.4 to 0.5 metres beneath the camera; a wooden floor, a small tray at the lower left, and a stool base at the lower right lie about 0.7 to 0.9 metres below. Another person is seated directly ahead, facing the camera wearer from roughly 0.5 to 0.8 metres away, but their head and torso extend beyond the upper edge of the view, so only their black-covered legs in the upper right and both forearms reaching forward are visible. A white UV/LED nail lamp rests on the armrest's left side, around 0.1 to 0.2 metres from the neighbouring grey towel pad to its right; the seated person's right hand sits inside the lamp and is mostly hidden, whereas their left hand reaches forward across the lamp and pad toward the bottom centre. Near the bottom border, roughly 0.3 to 0.4 metres from the camera, both of the camera wearer's hands directly touch the seated person's left thumb: the wearer's left hand grips the thumb together with a partly obscured dark bottle, and the right hand holds a blue-tipped brush. The hands, lamp, and cushion are comfortably reachable by either person. Moving through the five frames from left to right, the viewpoint drifts slightly downward and to the right, while the seated person's left hand slides several centimetres rightward off the lamp housing during the first three frames, then tilts a little in frame five as the brush withdraws a couple of centimetres toward the lower right.
depth: The depth image represents the manicure setup as layered top-down geometry. The camera wearer's two hands occupy the bottom foreground as the brightest, closest surfaces, about 0.3–0.4 m away, holding a nail-polish bottle and brush against the client's outstretched right hand at approximately 0.35–0.45 m. Immediately below and behind those hands, around 0.45–0.6 m away and rendered mid-light grey, are the rounded white UV/LED nail lamp on the left—with the client's left forearm extending into it from the upper left—the grey towel, and the beige padded armrest running from left to right; each is within reach of both client and camera wearer. More distant, toward the upper right at roughly 0.6–0.8 m and shown in medium grey, are the seated client's black-clothed legs angled toward the wearer. The wooden flooring and under-table tray in the lower corners appear darkest and farthest, about 1.0–1.2 m below, while neither person's torso or head is visible because both remain outside the frame. Over the five frames, the client's right hand changes from brilliant white in frames 1–2 to a somewhat darker grey in frames 3–5 as the wearer's head shifts slightly backward and the wearer's left thumb moves atop the client's finger, producing a distinct foreground occlusion edge. Relative to RGB alone, depth clearly reveals the vertical descent from the elevated hand and domed lamp to the armrest, legs, and floor. However, it is unreliable where the client's finger and wearer's thumb fuse into one saturated white mass in frames 1–2, and where the UV lamp's hollow interior is represented as a smooth, flattened surface.
segmentation: The segmentation view defines the spatial extents and overlaps of the main foreground areas, distinctly separating the client's centrally outstretched right hand and forearm, which descend from the top centre at about 0.35–0.5 m, from the camera wearer's bottom-positioned hands at roughly 0.3–0.4 m and the curved UV nail lamp on the left at around 0.45–0.55 m; all remain within both people's arm reach. The client's right arm appears above and overlaps the lamp and towel, while the camera wearer's left hand and brush partly block its fingertip from below. Meanwhile, the client's left wrist lies along the top-left boundary, and their legs at the top-right edge are mostly or completely absent from the segmentation against the black background, approximately 0.6–0.8 m distant. Through the five frames, the centre mask assigned to the client's right hand becomes narrower and moves slightly right relative to the lamp from frames 2 to 3, coinciding with an adjustment in camera angle and repositioning of the wearer's lower hands around the fingertip. Although its borders make the continuous outline of the client's extended forearm easier to distinguish from the similarly coloured beige cushion and towel, the semantic labels are very unreliable: the client's hand, UV lamp, and wearer's hands are repeatedly labelled 'banana,' while frames 1, 3, 4, and 5 combine the wearer's hands, towel, and lamp into single merged masks.
pose: The pose visualization tries to identify the articulated two-dimensional joints of the client's extended right hand at the scene's centre, approximately 0.35–0.5 m from the camera wearer and directed downward toward the bottom edge. Everything else is left entirely empty, including the client's torso and head outside the view, their left hand inside the lamp on the left, and the camera wearer's hands along the bottom. In frames 1, 2, and 5, a magenta hand skeleton follows the wrist from the top centre and branches downward through the fingers within the camera wearer's reach, corresponding to the hand's angle from the upper centre toward the lower foreground. Across all five frames, the detected hand landmarks move a little downward and draw closer together from frame 1 to frame 2, disappear completely and are replaced by incorrect yellow body skeletons in frames 3 and 4, then return slightly lower and farther to the right in frame 5. The magenta skeletons in frames 1, 2, and 5 help communicate the client's right hand's downward direction and spread fingers despite the fingertips being obscured by the camera wearer's grasp. Nevertheless, the map is broadly unreliable: it never detects the wearer's hands, turns the client's bent fingers into tangled lines that cross themselves, and invents a boxed yellow torso skeleton with clusters of facial dots over the UV lamp and hands in frames 3 and 4.
